source_title: Dragon Ball: It's the End of an Era For Akira Toriyama’s Legacy
source_excerpt:
Renan is the Anime Lead Editor for GameRant. Ren graduated Cum Laude from Lesley University in 2017 and has been focusing exclusively on his journalistic endeavors ever since. When Ren isn't working, he's usually playing video games or reading.
It's been over two years since Akira Toriyama passed away on March 1, 2024, and yet another page of the legendary mangaka's legacy is being turned. With the success of Dr. Slump in the early '80s, Akira Toriyama was able to found his own manga production studio, Bird Studio. Without Bird, you don't get Dragon Ball , Dragon Quest , or any other project Akira Toriyama worked on throughout his career. Bird Studio is an icon within the manga, anime, and video game industry, but it's also closing its doors forever.
Akira Toriyama's home base and where he penned his masterpiece Dragon Ball , Bird Studio is being demolished. Given just how important Bird Studio and Akira Toriyama are to modern art, it's a shame that the entire building is being taken down as opposed to being preserved as a historical or cultural landmark. Akira Toriyama's former collaborators have spoken up to express their sorrow over the demolition.
The Studio That Created Dragon Ball is Closing Its Doors Forever
The end of Bird Studio marks the end of a major part of Dragon Ball history. Even when the Dragon Ball Super manga returns, Toyotarou will not be able to continue the story in the same space it's been told since 1984. Akira Toriyama's first editor, Kazuhiko Torishima, responded to the news on X , writing, "The place I visited once a month / The place where all sorts of characters and work were born is disappearing / He really is gone."
Given that Torishima and Toriyama remained close even after Dragon Ball moved on to new editors, Bird Studio being demolished is likely very personal for him. The Chief Animation Director for Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero , Chikashi Kubota, who worked closely with Toriyama on the movie, also wrote, "It's too soon for Toriyama-sensei's home to get demolished. This is heartbreaking." According to Japanese locals, Bird Studio's demolation has been completed and is already gone.
